newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Banco Frances in capital increase - agency.
newsitem.headline: Banco Frances in capital increase - agency.

text.p: Argentina's Banco Frances will carry out a $300-$350 million capital increase to finance its purchase of 71.8 percent of Banco de Credito Argentino, the state-run Telam news agency said Tuesday.

Telam quoted an unnamed representative of Frances's controlling company, Spain's Banco de Bilbao Vizcaya, announcing the capital increase, but Frances Marketing Manager Guillermo Laje told Reuters the report was premature.
"We are still in the first stages of studying how to finance the operation and nothing has been decided by any means," Laje said.
He said that means of financing under consideration included "a capital increase, issuing of debt or a combination of both."
Frances did not disclose the value of its purchase announced Friday but banking sources put it at some $430 million.
They added Banco de Bilbao, which has a 30 percent controlling stake in Frances, is negotiating to buy all the shares of Credito for a total of about $600 million.
